reply:
Whether you need Self Assessment usually depends on your circumstances. If you were self-employed as a sole trader and earned more than £1,000 before reliefs in a tax year, you normally must register and send a tax return. The £1,000 trading allowance is a relief you may claim — it is not a free pass to ignore Self Assessment when your trading income is already above £1,000.

Roughly how much did you earn from self-employment / freelancing before expenses, and for which tax year?

Official guidance: https://www.gov.uk/self-assessment-tax-returns/who-must-send-a-tax-return

sources.title: PAYE employment plus additional income
sources.excerpt: Being taxed under PAYE does not automatically mean you have no Self Assessment obligations. Additional untaxed income, self-employment, property income or other criteria can still mean you need to file a return. Check GOV.UK ‘who must send a tax return’.

sources.title: Who needs to send a Self Assessment tax return
sources.excerpt: You usually need to send a Self Assessment tax return if you were self-employed, a partner in a partnership, had untaxed income, or received notice from HMRC to file. Being employed does not automatically remove the requirement if other criteria apply.

sources.title: Company directors and Self Assessment
sources.excerpt: Company directors often need to complete a Self Assessment tax return, for example for dividends, benefits, or other untaxed income. Corporation Tax for the company is separate from the director’s personal Self Assessment. Confirm on GOV.UK.
